correctness.rationale: For each rational beta and integer m the proposed matrix dimensions and probe count are integral; exact residual counts give strict Frobenius and log-variance pilot inequalities. The logarithmic inequalities follow from log(1+x) between x/(1+x) and x, with a<=1/4. Two-eigenvalue preconditioned matrices make m>=2 Lanczos exact; independent Gaussian fourth moments yield precise full-budget risks and an exact regret ratio diverging with rank. The packaged standard-library checker passes 27,860 finite supplementary assertions; no finite test is used for an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating preprint (arXiv:2601.05778, Sections 2 and 4) provides exact per-allocation Gaussian variance formulas and a two-rank decision heuristic, and even acknowledges occasional wrong decisions. It does not prove a two-plateau, every-rational-fraction, arbitrarily-near-identity family with unbounded full-budget regret while both exact oracle tests prefer one sample. A closely related published ideal allocation theorem was read in full and compares full-budget allocations, not the reduced-rank predictor. Source inspection plus mathematical implications support provisional non-coverage; unindexed equivalent constructions remain possible.
residual_risks: The nearest previous full-budget allocation theorem may be combined with the original pilot formulas to derive variants of this example, even though it does not itself state the two-rank failure.
Unindexed pilot-based stochastic trace allocation literature or textbooks may contain an equivalent adversarial two-plateau example.
The conclusion is for the deterministic ideal diagnostic and is not a probability statement about the implemented random Nyström diagnostic.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by a published adaptive log-determinant allocation rule, not by arbitrary spectrum fitting. The exact construction separates spectral-proxy error from more fundamental rank-extrapolation error, covers every fixed rational pilot fraction and the published recommended choice, keeps matrices positive definite and arbitrarily near identity, and isolates the effect from Lanczos quadrature error. These properties make a useful substantive counterexample for designing robust selection safeguards without asserting practical implementation failure.
